leads.title: Data Analyst Internship
leads.posting: About the Company Skill Orbit is building practical learning and career opportunities that help emerging professionals develop relevant, workplace-ready capabilities. This remote internship offers aspiring analysts the opportunity to work in a structured environment, learn from real business data, and contribute to meaningful reporting and analysis initiatives. Responsibilities Collect, clean, organize, and validate data from multiple sources. Use Excel to prepare analysis, summaries, pivot tables, charts, and recurring reports. Write SQL queries to retrieve, filter, join, and aggregate information from databases. Identify trends, inconsistencies, and useful insights in datasets. Support the preparation of dashboards, presentations, and data-driven recommendations. Document analytical processes and communicate findings clearly to stakeholders. Requirements Strong interest in data analysis, reporting, and business problem-solving. Working knowledge of Excel and SQL. Comfort with numbers, structured thinking, and attention to detail. Ability to learn quickly, manage tasks independently, and collaborate effectively in a remote environment. No prior professional experience is required; academic projects or practice work in analytics are welcome. This is a three-month, fully remote, paid internship with a monthly stipend of ₹20,000 to ₹35,000. Interns will gain practical exposure to data preparation, querying, analysis, and insight communication while working with a distributed team.

leads.title: Build for Bharat Fellow (AI/Engineering/Design)
leads.posting: Bharat Digital Anywhere The Build for Bharat Fellowship is a paid, six-month programme that places early-career engineers, designers and AI practitioners inside government departments. Fellows work alongside government teams on real projects, improving public systems used by millions of people. What fellows get: Real-world experience: Work on live government projects, interact with users and understand how public services operate. Learning and mentorship: An orientation, regular reviews and expert office hours with practitioners such as Kailash Nadh (CTO, Zerodha), Rukmini S (Founder, Data for India) and Devanshi Sihare (TinkerLabs). A community: Learn alongside other fellows and connect with people working in public technology. Some projects from past cohorts Official statistics: Built MoSPI’s eSankhyiki MCP server , making official statistics accessible to AI assistants. Rural libraries: Developed Arivu Mitra, a WhatsApp companion for Gram Panchayat librarians in Karnataka using Whatomate . Transport: Built a transit analytics dashboard for Chennai’s transport authority and NHAI's Annual Pass web and app which has helped sell 1 Cr Annual Passes in a year. Citizen services: Redesigned Tamil Nadu’s e-Sevai services, IRCTC ticket UI, e-swathu, etc., to improve the citizen experience. Explore more projects Fellowship at a glance Duration : January–June 2027 (6 months, on-site) Location: On-site at a partner government department Stipend: ₹40,000 per month Eligibility: Indian citizens graduating in 2027 or who completed their latest degree in 2024–2026, with demonstrable skills in Engineering, Design or AI Application deadline: 18 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST Apply here: https://bharatdigital.org/fellowship

Bharat Digital â Build for Bharat Fellowship Get Involved Programme Build for Bharat Fellowship 2027 Past Cohorts Past Projects Cohort 2027 Applications for 2027 are now live. Apply now Best viewed on Desktop × Home Fellowship Build for Bharat Fellowship 2027 Past Cohorts Past Projects About Get Involved Build for Bharat Fellowship 2027 A six-month paid fellowship inside a government department, working alongside government partners, solving tasks for real-world impact. Apply for 2027 cohort Read the FAQs We aim to identify and train early-career public-interest technologists who can strengthen, modernise and humanise the digital systems solving India's most urgent public and governance challenges. What the fellowship holds 01 Orientation and onboarding Before you start, an orientation in public service, policy and what it takes to put technology inside complex social systems. You hear from some of India’s top technologists, policymakers, designers and administrators. Much of it is tacit knowledge you won’t find anywhere else, there to ready you for the six months ahead. Watch last year’s orientation ↗ The 2026 cohort 02 Build Once deputed to a government team, you work alongside the people already there, on real problems and real codebases. Most fellows ship changes to government systems within their first month, and a few go on to redesign or launch services used by millions of Indians. This is the real thing, not a hackathon or a side-project. A session with an anganwadi group · RDPR Karnataka 03 Mentorship Throughout the fellowship, you have regular mentoring and check-ins with Bharat Digital’s core team. On top of that, you get office hours with some of India’s leading public-spirited technologists and designers. Previous mentors include Kailash Nadh (CTO, Zerodha), Rukmini S (Data for India; author of Whole Numbers and Half Truths ) and Devanshi Sihare (Head of Social Impact, TinkerLabs). Fellows with mentor Rukmini S · Data for India 04 Field visits Field visits are an integral part of the fellowship. Not a line of code gets changed until you’ve understood the problem first-hand: visited the offices and rooms where your technology will be used, and met the people it will affect. By the end, you won’t just have immersed yourself in India’s grassroots; you’ll understand how public systems are actually conceived, and how they touch the ground. StoryWeaver Lite with children in a Gram Panchayat library · RDPR Karnataka 05 Community building We believe deeply in the power of community. We create opportunities for fellows to get to know one another across cohorts, and to plug into the wider public-technology ecosystem through events, talks and one-on-one sessions with founders and practitioners. A mixer for the 2025 and 2026 cohorts 06 Public technology careers Six months inside a department changes what you can do next, and often what you want to do next. We work closely with you to find that next step, so you can keep building in the public-technology ecosystem: in government, in research labs, or at the leading tech-for-good organisations using technology to improve public systems. leads.title: Graduate Transport Planner
leads.posting: At Curtins, we're an employee-owned engineering consultancy driven by a simple ambition: to create a better built environment for everyone. For over 65 years, we've delivered practical, innovative and sustainable solutions that make a positive impact on communities across the UK and Ireland. From major regeneration schemes and commercial developments to education, healthcare and residential projects, our work helps shape the places where people live, learn, work and thrive. As a Graduate Transport Planner, you'll work alongside experienced planners, engineers and consultants, contributing to a wide range of projects while developing the technical and professional skills you need to build your career. Whether you're interested in transport assessments, active travel & sustainable mobility, highways or public transport, we'll give you the experience, guidance and support to find the areas that interest you most and develop your expertise in development planning. What you'll be doing You will support the planning and development process, helping clients bring projects forward from initial concept through to planning approval. Your responsibilities will include: Assisting with the preparation of Transport Assessments and Transport Statements. Supporting the production of Travel Plans and technical planning reports. Analysing traffic, transport and movement data. Assisting with junction assessments and development impact studies. Supporting planning applications for residential, commercial and mixed-use developments. Working alongside planners, civil engineers and other specialists to deliver integrated solutions. Attending client meetings, project discussions and stakeholder consultations. Taking part in wider Curtins activities including STEM outreach, charity initiatives and community projects. What kind of projects will I get to work on? You'll be involved in projects across a wide range of sectors, including: Residential developments. Urban regeneration schemes.
